name: Bricklaying
description: This course covers the practical skills you need to lay bricks and blocks on a construction site. You will learn to mix mortar, set out walls, build to line and level, and construct corners, openings and jambs. The training also covers reading simple drawings, choosing the right tools and materials, and working safely around scaffolding and plant. By the end, learners can complete basic bricklaying work to a standard that holds up under inspection, with a certificate issued in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable.
outcomes: Lay bricks and blocks to line and level using strings, levels and corner blocks
Mix mortar to the right consistency for different wall types
Build straight walls, corners, openings and jambs from a simple drawing
Identify and use bricklaying tools and materials correctly
Work safely on site and keep the work area clean and tidy
audience: New entrants who want to start a career in construction
General workers on building sites who want to add a trade skill
Small contractors and home builders who want to improve quality and speed
Supervisors who need to check bricklaying work against a standard

faqs.q: How much does bricklaying training cost?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the size of your group and the delivery mode, so the course is quoted per booking. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za for a quote and we will come back to you with a figure. Group bookings are negotiable. Training can run online, at our centres in Midrand or Durban, or on site at your premises.

faqs.q: How long does the bricklaying course take?
faqs.a: The duration is quoted when you book, because it depends on group size and delivery mode. A small group at our Midrand or Durban centre may finish faster than a large group trained on site. Daily classes run with no waiting period, so you can start as soon as a date suits. Email info@rehtraining.co.za or call 010 746 6954 to arrange your dates.

faqs.q: Do I need experience before I can do bricklaying training?
faqs.a: No, the course suits beginners and workers with some site experience. The trainer takes you through the basics step by step, and practical work happens under supervision. If you already lay bricks at work, the course is a good way to have your skills checked against a standard and to pick up better techniques.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site in Johannesburg or Durban?
faqs.a: Yes. On-site training at your premises is one of our standard delivery modes, and it suits contractors who need a whole team trained at once. We also run daily classes at our centres in Midrand and Durban, and online theory where it applies. Email info@rehtraining.co.za with your location and group size, and we will put together a plan and a quote.

name: Formwork
description: This course covers the erection and stripping of formwork for columns, beams, slabs and walls. Learners work with timber and steel shutters, learn to set out and align formwork to line and level, and apply release agents and supports correctly. The training includes reading simple drawings, checking formwork before concrete is placed, and stripping and cleaning shutters safely. The outcome is a worker who can carry out formwork tasks to tolerance on a live construction site, with certification in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable.
outcomes: Set out and erect formwork for columns, beams, slabs and walls
Work with timber and steel shutters, including release agents and supports
Read simple drawings and check formwork dimensions before concrete is placed
Strip, clean and store formwork without damaging it or the concrete
Apply safe handling and housekeeping rules on a formwork deck
audience: General construction workers moving into structural work
Carpenters and joiners who want formal recognition of formwork skills
Team leaders who supervise concrete and formwork gangs
Contractors taking on residential or commercial building projects

faqs.q: How much does formwork training cost?
faqs.a: Formwork training is quoted per booking, because the price depends on group size and delivery mode. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za and we will send you a quote, usually within a day. Prices are negotiable for group bookings. You can train online, at our centres in Midrand or Durban, or on site at your premises.

faqs.q: How long does the formwork course take?
faqs.a: The duration depends on the group and the delivery mode, so it is quoted when you book. Daily classes run at our centres, which means no waiting period before you start. On-site training for a crew can be scheduled around your project programme. Contact us on email info@rehtraining.co.za or call 010 746 6954, and we will confirm dates and duration.

faqs.a: No, the course suits anyone working with formwork, including general workers, steel fixers and site supervisors. name: Steel Fixing
description: This course covers cutting, bending and tying reinforcing steel to match drawings and bar schedules. Learners practise placing reinforcement for columns, beams, slabs and footings, setting laps, cover and chairs correctly, and fixing steel so it stays in position while concrete is placed. The training also covers handling steel safely and checking work before a concreting team arrives. The outcome is a steel fixer who can produce sound reinforcement work on site, with a certificate issued in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable.
outcomes: Read bar schedules and simple reinforcement drawings
Cut and bend reinforcing steel to the required shapes and lengths
Tie reinforcement for footings, columns, beams and slabs with correct laps and cover
Use chairs, spacers and supports to keep steel in position
Handle and store steel safely and keep the fixing area tidy
audience: General workers who want to move into structural steel work
Site labourers looking for a certified trade skill
Team leaders and supervisors who check reinforcement work
Contractors who need a reliable fixing gang on their projects

name: Concrete Works
description: This course covers concrete from mix design to finished surface. Learners practise mixing concrete to the right proportions, placing and compacting it in formwork, and finishing, curing and protecting surfaces. The training also covers quality checks, slump testing basics, and the safe handling of concrete and admixtures on site. The outcome is a worker who can carry out concrete works to specification and spot problems before they harden into defects, with certification aligned to SAQA unit standards where applicable.

Place and compact concrete in formwork without segregation
Finish surfaces to a level, smooth standard and cure them properly
Carry out basic quality checks, including slump testing
Handle concrete, cement and admixtures safely on site

Small contractors who place concrete without specialist crews
Supervisors who need to check concrete quality and curing
Workers moving from labouring into a certified construction skill

The outcome is a worker who understands stormwater drainage and can carry out installation and maintenance work to a sound standard.
